value.title: Continue assertively
value.meaning: Continue a brief point when voices overlap.
value.risk: Repeatedly talking over others can appear domineering.
value.example: “Let me finish this connection briefly, and then I’d like to hear other perspectives.”

value.title: Request to go first
value.meaning: Acknowledge the other speaker and ask to make your point first.
value.advantage: Preserves an opportunity while recognizing another person.
value.risk: Repeated requests can control the floor. Honor the promised next turn.
value.example: “Would you mind if I finish this point first? I’d like to hear you afterward.”

value.title: Yield and request the next turn
value.meaning: Let the other person go first, then ask to contribute.
value.risk: The discussion may move on before your point fits.
value.example: “Go ahead. I’d like to build on that afterward.”

value.title: Claim a direct connection
value.meaning: Explain why your point responds immediately to the previous speaker.
value.risk: Repeated urgency claims can dominate the floor.
value.example: “Could I respond briefly to that concern before we change topics?”

records.value:
MIDDLE STAGE QUICK REFERENCE
1. CONTRIBUTE SUBSTANCE
• Share relevant research. Cite publication and date.
• Explain why evidence matters. Use anecdotes to illustrate, not replace, evidence.
2. SUPPORT THE GROUP
• Take notes and look up regularly. Track time, invite perspectives, and redirect respectfully.
3. COMMUNICATE PROFESSIONALLY
• Address fellow discussants. Speak within your role and finish sentences audibly.
4. MANAGE SPEAKING CONFLICTS
• Balance assertiveness with collaboration. Honor promised turns.
5. YOUR GOAL
Contribute evidence. Build on others. Keep the group moving toward a solution.
These coaching strategies do not replace official tournament rules.
